newsitem.title: SOMALIA: 17 people reported killed in Somali fighting.
newsitem.headline: 17 people reported killed in Somali fighting.

text.p: At least 17 people were killed in fighting between militiamen loyal to faction leader Hussein Aideed and clan rivals in a town in southern Somalia, witnessess said on Tuesday.
Speaking by radio from Qansahdhere, they said fighters of the Rahanwein Resistance Army (RRA) infiltrated the town on Monday and clashed with Aideed's militiamen. At least 17 people were killed.
A spokesman for the RRA said its fighters had captured the town and the surrounding area and killed 12 of Aideed's gunmen.
But an Aideed official said Qansahdhere remained under the control of his forces after "bandits" had been chased away.

Qansahdhere is 70 km (40 miles) southwest of Baidoa town, seized by Aideed's forces in September 1995. The RRA has mounted intermittent hit-and-run attacks since then in a failed campaign to seize it back.

Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of late dictator president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991. Aideed was elected president by supporters last year but rival faction leaders have rejected the move and his administration.
